title: Oedipus on Broadway #oedipus #markstrong #lesleymanville #theatrerevi...
transcript: Direct from London comes a modern adaptation of Oedipus that I found entertaining but not life-changing. In this version by Robert Icke, politician Oedipus is on the verge of a landslide victory when an uninvited guest makes a few claims about Oedipus that send him spiraling. I won't spoil it here, though I imagine the expectation is that most of the audience will be familiar with the basic story, since the foreshadowing is so obvious that it seems intentionally comical. I thought the production was well done and I thought the writing was clever and satisfying, but I couldn't quite get behind the political framing and the overall concept here. It feels a little contrived at the expense of the allegorical nature of the story. This is also not helped by the clock on the stage counting down to what you know will inevitably be the climax of the whole thing. On one hand, it's an interesting device to build tension, but I mostly found it distracting and felt like it undermined the performances and sound design that were more than capable of building tension on their own. To that point though, the performances are what kept me engaged from beginning to end. Mark Strong and Lesley Manville are great as Oedipus and Jocasta, but I also really enjoyed Olivia Reis as Antigone — I wouldn't mind seeing a modern adaptation of that play with her in the role. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Creator calls it entertaining but not life-changing, praises performances and writing but criticizes the political framing, concept, and countdown clock device. Lands squarely in mixed territory.
